title.en: Poem by Wang Wei in the Cursive Script Style

museum_text.en:
Poem and painting, once mounted together as one fan, exemplify the collaboration between imperial patron and court painter. Emperor Lizong’s calligraphy cites a verse from Wang Wei’s (701–761) poem, Walking to where the water ends, I sit and watch when clouds arise.

Ma Lin’s response is this painting. At the water’s edge, a scholar reclines by a large rock. The view leads across the empty middle ground to a distant mountain. With sparse ink and subtly graded washes, Ma Lin visualizes the poetic verse. The painting suggests the impact of Chan aesthetics through interaction between the palace, literati-officials, and monasteries around Hangzhou.

The leaf facing Emperor Lizong’s calligraphy has an inscription by Zhang Daqian (1899–1983).

Emperor Lizong had little interest in governmental affairs, but he was perhaps the finest calligrapher among the Song emperors.

intro.zh: 南宋理宗皇帝写下唐代诗人王维（701–761）的两句诗：“行到水穷处，坐看云起时。”
intro.en: Emperor Lizong of the Southern Song wrote out two lines by the Tang poet Wang Wei (701–761): 'Walking to where the water ends, I sit and watch when clouds arise.'

intro.zh: 这幅书法和马麟据诗意所画的一幅画，原本裱在同一把扇子上。
intro.en: This calligraphy and a painting by Ma Lin that visualises the verse were once mounted together as one fan.

intro.zh: 上方的葫芦形印章刻有干支“丙辰”，即1256年。
intro.en: The gourd-shaped seal at the top carries the cyclical date bingchen, 1256.

intro.zh: 理宗对朝政不太关心，馆方却称他也许是宋代皇帝中最好的书法家。
intro.en: Lizong took little interest in government, but the museum calls him perhaps the finest calligrapher among the Song emperors.

look_for.zh: 从右往左读两行字：行到水窮處／坐看雲起時。
look_for.en: Read the two columns from right to left: 行到水窮處 / 坐看雲起時.

look_for.zh: 圆圆的形状：它原本是一把团扇，后来才裱成册页。
look_for.en: The round shape: it was once a fan, and is now mounted as an album leaf.

look_for.zh: 左边的小款和红色印章。
look_for.en: The small signature and red seals at the left.

alt.zh: 一面裱在白色纸上的圆形褐色绢扇，上面有两行黑色书法，左边有红色印章。
alt.en: A round fan of brownish silk mounted on a white page, with two columns of black calligraphy and red seals at the left.

views.zh: 大都会博物馆的评价更谨慎：理宗是高宗之后宋代皇帝中最好的书法家。
views.en: The Met puts it more narrowly: Lizong was the finest calligrapher among the Song emperors who came after Gaozong.

note.zh: 每一句都对照所注出处核对过；找不到可靠出处的说法已删去或改写。
note.en: Every sentence was checked against the sources it cites; claims without a reliable source were cut or rewritten.
